title: Israel election: Exit polls show no clear winner, with Netanyahu's fate unclear
summary: While Netanyahu's party is projected to be the biggest in parliament, two out of three exit polls show his bloc even with the opposition. No bloc has a clear majority. DW has the latest.
byline: Patrick Große, Mark Hallam, Felix Tamsut, Roshni Majumdar, Matt Ford

image.caption: Supporters of the main opposition party Yashar celebrate after exit polls suggested they were on course to win 21 seatsImage: Jack Guez/AFP

blocks.text: Netanyahu calls for 'strong' right-wing government after election

blocks.caption: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu addresses supporters after Tuesday's electionImage: David Goldman/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has vowed to form a new right-wing government, despite exit polls showing no clear majority for either political bloc.
"We are still waiting for the real results," Netanyahu told cheering supporters in a speech early Wednesday, stressing that his Likud party was the largest in Israel.
"We must put in place a strong government of the right," he said.
Netanyahu also rejected the prospect of a government relying on the support of Arab parties, which made strong gains in Tuesday's election.
Turning to security, Netanyahu said Israel had a "unique opportunity" together with US President Donald Trump to end what he called the Iranian threat.

Updated exit polls show Netanyahu's bloc and the opposition led by Gadi Eisenkot either tied or separated by a narrow margin. Neither side is projected to win the 61 seats needed for a majority in the 120-seat Knesset.
